task: Survey of datasets, benchmarks and data curation for agentic RAG
problem: Agentic RAG needs hard tasks requiring planning, retrieval and multiple reasoning decisions plus rich interactive trajectories; such data are scarce, costly to annotate and error-prone when synthesised.
architecture: Organises agentic RAG around a data lifecycle - data collecting, preprocessing and task formulation, task construction (generate-verify-filter/refine), data for evaluation, and data enhancement for SFT and RL - and catalogues training datasets and benchmarks for QA, web and software-engineering domains.
key_results: Contrasts traditional and agentic RAG along the data lifecycle: static corpora vs interactive data, single-step vs decomposable hard tasks, correctness-only vs multi-axis evaluation, CoT vs thought-action trajectories and process rewards.
Groups difficulty-enhancement methods into complexity, uncertainty and expertise, and notes that classic single-hop QA datasets such as NQ and TriviaQA are near saturation.
strengths: First survey focusing on data curation for agentic RAG; useful catalogue of benchmarks and training data by domain.

limitations.text: Covers text-based data only, not multimodal data pipelines.
Conceptual; no large-scale quantitative benchmarking or unified evaluation across datasets.

title: Data-Centric Perspectives on Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey
